headline: The UK government has launched a challenge worth up to £80 million to test nine new technologies, some using AI, that could speed up dementia diagnosis in the NHS.
score_reason: Official UK programme, but announced on 6 Oct 2026 and only some of the nine projects use AI; lowered by 1 from 5.
importance_line: Could shorten waits for people with possible dementia and their families, but the tools are still to be tested in real NHS settings and only some of the nine are described as using AI.
source: UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), via News-Medical
summary: UK Research and Innovation says nine projects will be tested in the NHS with up to £80 million, aiming for 92% of people to be diagnosed within 18 weeks of referral, up from around 60% today; they include a home-monitoring platform called Minder that uses sensors and AI, and a Cambridge AI tool that predicts how dementia will progress. Projects receive further funding only if they prove they work.
notes: Digital Health (pool source) was blocked by Cloudflare; read the UKRI release as carried by News-Medical on 6 Oct 2026.
